title: One keen instance per directory: derive tmux socket from startup cwd
description: Running keen in a second project currently reattaches the single global tmux server (socket 'keen', session 'keen'), showing the first project's sessions. Wanted: one keen instance per exact startup directory, silently — keen in dir A boots/reattaches A's instance, keen in dir B gets B's. Implementation: derive the private tmux socket name from the symlink-resolved absolute cwd (basename + short hash), so each directory gets a fully isolated server. KEEN_TMUX_SOCKET env still overrides. 'keen kill' kills only the current directory's server.
close_reason: Implemented: tmux socket derived from startup cwd (keen-<basename>-<hash8>); KEEN_TMUX_SOCKET still overrides; keen kill scoped to current dir's server. Unit tests for socket derivation + live two-dir verification (independent boot/reattach/kill, existing global instance untouched).

title: Sidebar beads: two-line rows styled like bd list
description:
Render each bd-ready bead in the sidebar as TWO lines, echoing bd list's row style:

  ○ cmdr-keen-gu3 ● P4
    Placeholder: second demo bead

Line 1: bd status circle (○ open — the only status bd ready emits today, but map ◐ in_progress / ● blocked / ✓ closed / ❄ deferred defensively), the issue id, and a priority badge ('● P4') colored by priority. Line 2: the title, faint, indented under the id.

No bd-status legend in the sidebar (the circle is self-explanatory). Layout math (BeadRowsToShow / showLegend) must account for 2 rows per bead.
close_reason: Shipped: two-line bd-list-style sidebar rows (landed in 2e8a786) + bd list polling. Closing also demos a bead dropping off the sidebar.
